title: Tech E&O vs Cyber Insurance for SaaS Startups
summary: Compare Tech E&O and Cyber for SaaS startups: software errors, data breaches, downtime, AI outputs, package costs and customer contracts.
body_markdown:
These are hypothetical examples built to make the comparison practical. They are not customer claims or coverage decisions.


### 1. Your billing integration applies the wrong discount


A SaaS startup ships a billing integration that applies a discount twice. Its customer discovers a month of underbilling and demands compensation for the resulting loss.


Start with Tech E&O: the allegation is that the startup's technology work caused the customer's financial loss. Review whether the product and integration services are described in the policy, along with the treatment of the customer's demand, contractual obligations and defense costs. The startup's own cost to rewrite the code is a separate question.


### 2. A stolen account exposes customer records


An attacker uses a compromised administrator account to download customer records. The startup needs to investigate, work out who was affected and respond to customer claims.


Start with Cyber, then separate the costs. Investigation and notification are first-party response questions. Claims alleging a failure to protect data are third-party liability questions. Ask which of these are included, which need an endorsement and whether any sublimits apply.


### 3. Ransomware takes the product offline


A ransomware incident stops a SaaS platform for two days. The startup incurs recovery costs and loses subscription revenue. A customer also alleges that the outage caused a missed delivery deadline and lost sales.


There are two balance sheets to consider. The startup's recovery and lost income call for a review of its first-party Cyber and business-interruption terms. The customer's demand calls for a separate review of liability coverage, including how the Tech E&O and Cyber forms treat a security-related outage. Check waiting periods, shared limits and exclusions before assuming one policy handles every part.


### 4. An AI feature sends the wrong purchasing recommendation


A SaaS product's AI feature recommends an incorrect inventory order. A customer follows it, then alleges a financial loss when the stock cannot be sold.


Bring the AI feature into the coverage review explicitly. Corgi lists an AI and Algorithmic Liability endorsement among its available Tech E&O add-ons. Review the selected modules and wording for your actual product. Buying standard Tech E&O or Cyber alone does not answer whether an AI-output claim is included.
